summary: BC Forest Service lookout on Pilot Mountain near Prince George: a 1934 start per a 1946 newsletter, 1930s radio link, vandalism in 1977 and 1981. Present state not found.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia measures from the city limits (17 km, 11 mi); the 1977 newspaper gives 12 miles northwest of Prince George with no stated reference point.

The Canada Lookouts page carries a 'Bulkley - Nechako' label, but its own text (12 miles northwest of Prince George) and Wikipedia (Regional District of Fraser-Fort George) support Fraser-Fort George, the brief's local_unit, which is kept.

notes_for_editor: History comes from newsletter and newspaper extracts on the Canada Lookouts page, which are dated 1913 to 1981. Present status is unknown: no dated source says whether the lookout building still stands or whether it is open to visitors; the story says so. A Facebook group post surfaced in search (not fetched; snippet only) says the tower was removed in the mid-1990s with a question mark on the year; unverified and not used. Start-date conflict: the 1913 report names a lookout station, while the 1946 newsletter gives 1934 as the establishment year; the story reports both without choosing. Elevation differs slightly (Canada Lookouts 991 m, Wikipedia 995 m); not used. The brief's coordinates match Wikipedia and the Canada Lookouts page. Fact-check 2026-10-20: the 12-mile figure and the 1977 vandalism come from a Prince George Citizen item dated May 31, 1977; the shotgun blast and gate suggestion are a separate Prince George Citizen item dated May 20, 1981, so the story calls it a newspaper item. The July 1936 radio item and the November 1, 1946 tribute are both on the Canada Lookouts page. Wikipedia gives no date for the radio-site use, so 'now' was dropped from that claim.
